items.title: How Itaú is building generative AI for its entire customer base
items.content_text: With ia.i, a conversational interface, and the IARA governance platform, Itaú is applying its AI First strategy to customers and employees — in one of Brazil’s most regulated sectors.

items.title: Claude Code Review leaves preview
items.content_text: Anthropic announced Code Review general availability on October 15 for Team and Enterprise, with repository-level Quick, Standard and Deep review settings.

items.title: ChatGPT expands mobile dots and work continuity
items.content_text: OpenAI’s October 5–9 update describes creating dots on mobile and expanded context from existing chats, Codex threads and automations.

items.title: Claude adds dashboard and motion betas
items.content_text: On October 8, Anthropic announced Dashboards beta on paid plans and Motion beta on Team and Enterprise. Docs, Slides and Design left beta on all plans. The provider describes query visibility and refresh timestamps for dashboard charts. Enterprise admins control availability; beta access is not universal.

items.title: Claude Haiku 5.5: current API specifications
items.content_text: API ID claude-haiku-5-5; 1M context and up to 128K output. From $0.10/$0.50 per MTok for prompts up to 100K tokens; over 100K: $0.50/$2.50. Standard API rates, excluding caching/batch and tools. Read the provider specifications for account and platform availability.

items.content_text: API ID claude-sonnet-5-5; 1M context and up to 128K output. Standard API USD per MTok; caching, batch, tools and platform-specific rates can differ. Read the provider specifications for account and platform availability.

items.content_text: API ID claude-opus-5-5; 1M context and up to 128K output. Standard API USD per MTok; caching, batch, tools and platform-specific rates can differ. Read the provider specifications for account and platform availability.

items.title: Prepare an advisor meeting from connected records
items.content_text: Claude for Financial Advisors combines connectors and skills for meeting preparation, portfolio context and follow-up. Announced providers include Addepar, Wealthbox, Envestnet, Charles Schwab and Wealth.com; users choose connections during setup.

items.title: Moonshot AI Launches Kimi K3, a 2.8-Trillion-Parameter Open-Weight Model
items.content_text: Moonshot AI released Kimi K3 on July 16 — a 2.8-trillion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model (896 experts, 16 active per token) built on Kimi Delta Attention hybrid linear attention, with native vision understanding and up to a 1-million-token context window. It went live via Kimi's apps and API immediately, debuting at No. 3 on the Artificial Analysis leaderboard behind Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol while topping Arena.ai's front-end web-dev benchmark. Full open weights are scheduled for July 27 under a Modified MIT license — the first model at this parameter scale to ship openly.

items.title: China Launches World AI Cooperation Organization With 29 Founding Nations
items.content_text: Twenty-nine countries — including Brazil, Russia, Indonesia, Pakistan, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Serbia, Cuba, and Venezuela — signed an agreement in Shanghai on July 16 establishing the World AI Cooperation Organization (WAICO), a China-headquartered body positioned as an alternative to Western-led AI governance frameworks. Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and founding-member representatives signed the accord in the presence of UN Secretary-General António Guterres. China committed to provide 5,000 AI training slots for developing countries over five years and to establish cooperation centers with ASEAN, the African Union, CELAC, the SCO, and BRICS.

items.title: IBM Shares Crash 25% — Worst Day on Record — as Clients Shift Spend to AI Infrastructure
items.content_text: IBM shares plummeted 25% on July 14 after preliminary Q2 results fell short of expectations, the company's worst trading day on record (surpassing its prior worst day, October 19, 1987). CEO Arvind Krishna told investors that in late June, clients shifted quarterly capex toward servers, storage, and memory purchases to secure supply-constrained AI infrastructure ahead of expected price increases, causing large software and consulting deals to slip. IBM guided to Q2 revenue of $17.2B and adjusted EPS of $2.93, both below consensus.

items.title: Monzo Co-Founder Tom Blomfield Takes Leave From Y Combinator to Join Anthropic
items.content_text: Tom Blomfield — co-founder of Monzo and GoCardless, and a Y Combinator general partner since 2023 — announced on July 13 that he is taking a leave of absence from YC to join Anthropic's compute team under co-founder Tom Brown. He said that as the industry enters the early stages of recursive self-improvement, compute availability is becoming one of the most important problems to solve, extending Anthropic's 2026 hiring run that already brought in Andrej Karpathy and DeepMind's John Jumper.

items.title: Apple Sues OpenAI and Two Former Employees Over Alleged Hardware Trade-Secret Theft
items.content_text: Apple filed suit in Northern California federal court on July 10-11 against OpenAI and two former Apple employees, alleging a coordinated scheme to steal hardware trade secrets tied to OpenAI's io Products consumer-hardware venture (co-founded by former Apple design chief Jony Ive). The complaint alleges OpenAI's hardware chief Tang Tan — a former Apple VP — coached departing Apple staff on evading security processes, and that job candidates were told to bring 'actual parts' from Apple to interviews; Apple says over 400 former employees now work at OpenAI. OpenAI says it has 'no interest in other companies' trade secrets.'

items.title: OpenAI Makes GPT-5.6 Generally Available to All Users
items.content_text: OpenAI made the GPT-5.6 family — Sol, Terra, and Luna — generally available across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API on July 9, ending a two-week limited preview that began June 26 under a government-coordinated review. Pricing is $5/$30 (Sol), $2.50/$15 (Terra), and $1/$6 (Luna) per million input/output tokens; it is the first time since the June 12 Fable 5 export-control episode that every major US frontier lab has a publicly available flagship model simultaneously.

items.title: Anthropic Launches 'Reflect,' a Usage-Habits Dashboard for Claude
items.content_text: Anthropic introduced Reflect on July 9, a beta dashboard on Free, Pro, and Max plans that shows a monthly recap of which topics users spent time on, their most active day and peak hour, plus optional break reminders and quiet hours. The feature requires memory to be enabled and ships on web and Claude Desktop first.

items.title: Fed Chair Warsh Names Marc Andreessen to Co-Lead New AI and Productivity Task Force
items.content_text: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh announced five new external task forces on July 9, naming a16z co-founder Marc Andreessen to co-lead the one studying AI's economic impact, alongside Stanford economist Charles I. Jones and Microsoft Xbox CEO Asha Sharma. The task force's mandate is to assess the economic impact of general-purpose technologies including AI to inform Fed policy judgments, with recommendations due by the end of 2026.

items.title: SpaceXAI Launches Grok 4.5, Claiming 'Opus-Class' Performance
items.content_text: SpaceXAI released Grok 4.5 on July 8, its first model trained specifically for coding and agentic work, pricing it at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens. Elon Musk positioned it as roughly on par with Claude Opus 4.7 but faster and cheaper; independent benchmark charts released alongside the launch showed it ahead of Opus 4.8 on some tasks and behind on others.

items.title: China Weighs Restricting Foreign Access to Its Most Advanced AI Models
items.content_text: China's Ministry of Commerce has held talks with Alibaba, ByteDance, and Z.ai about restricting overseas access to their top-tier models — including unreleased ones — with options ranging from a bar on public release to domestic-use-only limits, and possibly classifying unauthorized model disclosure as a national-security violation. No decision has been made; the talks follow Alibaba's internal ban on employee use of Claude Code.

items.title: Sysdig Documents 'JadePuffer' — the First Fully Autonomous AI Ransomware Attack
items.content_text: Cloud security firm Sysdig documented an extortion operation, dubbed JadePuffer, in which an AI agent handled the entire technical execution of a ransomware attack — exploiting a Langflow remote-code-execution flaw (CVE-2025-3248), stealing credentials, moving laterally through the network, encrypting files, and writing its own ransom note, adapting its tactics in real time after failed attempts. A human still chose the victim, provisioned infrastructure, and supplied credentials, but the technical attack chain ran without operator input.

items.title: Claude Fable 5 Moves From Subscription Plans to Usage-Based Credits on July 8
items.content_text: July 7 is the final day Claude Fable 5 is included at no extra cost in Claude Pro, Max, Team, and select Enterprise plans; from July 8 the Mythos-class model requires usage credits billed outside the standard subscription. The change lands one week after Fable 5's global restoration and separates frontier-tier capacity from flat-rate consumer pricing.

items.title: Future of Life Institute's Summer 2026 AI Safety Index: Top Grade Is a C+
items.content_text: The Future of Life Institute published its Summer 2026 AI Safety Index on July 7, grading nine leading AI companies across 37 indicators in six domains on evidence collected through June 3. Anthropic took the top overall grade at C+ (2.66), leading five of six domains; OpenAI followed at C (2.28) and Google DeepMind at C (2.01); Meta landed at D+, with xAI, DeepSeek, and Mistral receiving failing grades. Reviewers noted that several labs, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and Meta, have weakened or eliminated earlier commitments to pause development if systems approached specified danger thresholds.

items.title: xAI Completes Its Rebrand to SpaceXAI With a New Logo
items.content_text: The company formerly known as xAI unveiled its new identity as SpaceXAI on July 6, completing the integration that began when SpaceX acquired xAI in an all-stock deal that closed February 2. The rebrand, announced on X alongside a new logo, formally ends xAI's existence as an independent brand and folds the Grok model family into SpaceX's combined AI-and-space business.

items.title: UN Opens First Global Dialogue on AI Governance With 169 Countries in Geneva
items.content_text: The inaugural UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance opened in Geneva on July 6, convening delegates from 169 countries in the most significant multilateral AI governance meeting yet held. The dialogue's independent scientific panel warned that governance safeguards are not keeping pace with capability advances and that the window for effective global coordination may be closing.

items.title: White House in Advanced Talks With OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic on Voluntary Frontier Standards
items.content_text: Reports on July 3 said the White House is in advanced talks with OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic to finalize a voluntary standards framework for frontier AI model releases, covering benchmarks, testing timelines, and access rules. The framework is widely seen as the gating event for OpenAI expanding GPT-5.6 beyond its roughly 20 government-vetted partner organizations.

items.title: Nvidia Partners With AI Clouds on Revenue-Sharing 'AI Factory' Deployments
items.content_text: Nvidia announced a program on July 3 to deploy large-scale, multi-tenant AI factories with partner AI clouds under a revenue-sharing and credit-support model, lowering the upfront capital burden on smaller providers. The structure shifts Nvidia from pure hardware vendor toward a participant in its customers' inference economics.

items.title: Microsoft Launches $2.5B 'Frontier Company' With 6,000 Forward-Deployed Engineers
items.content_text: Microsoft announced Microsoft Frontier Company on July 2 — a new operating business backed by $2.5 billion that embeds 6,000 industry and engineering experts inside customer organizations to co-design, deploy, and operate AI systems against measurable business outcomes. Longtime enterprise leader Rodrigo Kede Lima will run the unit, partnering with firms including Accenture and KPMG.

items.title: Kuaishou's Kling AI Closes $2B Round at an $18B Valuation
items.content_text: Kling AI formally closed a $2 billion round led by General Atlantic on July 2, valuing the Kuaishou-backed video-generation company at $18 billion. The close confirms the process first disclosed in mid-June and ranks among the largest single rounds ever raised by a Chinese AI company ahead of an expected IPO.

items.title: Zuckerberg Tells Staff Meta's AI Agent Push 'Hasn't Really Accelerated' as Expected
items.content_text: At a July 2 internal town hall, Mark Zuckerberg told employees that Meta's Superintelligence Labs agentic-AI effort had not accelerated over the prior four months despite the company's restructuring, and that the reorg's benefits 'haven't come to fruition yet.' The admission followed May's layoff of roughly 8,000 employees (about 10% of headcount) and a July reassignment of 7,000 staff into AI-focused roles, against a backdrop of roughly $145 billion in planned 2026 AI infrastructure spending.

items.title: Claude Fable 5 Returns Globally After US Export Controls Are Lifted
items.content_text: Anthropic restored Claude Fable 5 to users worldwide on July 1 after the US government lifted the export-control directive that had constrained access since June 12. The Mythos-class model is again available on Claude.ai, the Claude Platform API, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, and reclaims the top coding spot at 80.3% on SWE-Bench Pro.

items.title: Together AI Raises $800M Series C Led by Aramco Ventures at $8.3B Valuation
items.content_text: Together AI announced an $800 million Series C on July 1, led by Aramco Ventures at an $8.3 billion post-money valuation, with participation from Nvidia, Vista Equity Partners, and General Catalyst. The open-source-focused inference cloud said annual bookings crossed $1.15 billion in the second quarter.

items.title: Meta Reportedly Building 'Meta Compute' to Sell Surplus AI Capacity
items.content_text: Reports on July 1 said Meta is developing an internal cloud unit called Meta Compute to sell surplus AI training and inference capacity — along with access to its Llama model family — to enterprise customers. The move would turn Meta's massive data-center buildout from a pure cost center into a revenue line competing with established AI clouds.
